title: Session Chorus — feature inkling and rough PRD
body:
High-level idea (one-liner): Session Chorus = a lightweight aggregation layer that exposes curated, time-windowed context 'lanes' from a user’s previous sessions and related ephemeral signals, surfaced to the model as compact, scored snippets. Aim: better continuity + lower token cost than naive full-session stitching.

Motivation / problem statements (notes):
- Users expect continuity across short-lived sessions (e.g., several chat windows in same day) but we can’t always persist full KV for cost and privacy reasons.
- Current approaches either: send full recent history (expensive), rely on brittle heuristics (context loss), or require customers to wire their own datastore.
- Need a solution that is: incremental, configurable per-tenant, respects privacy/retention rules, and gives predictable token/econ tradeoffs.

Core hypothesis: A small, scored set of 3–7 'chorus lanes' (e.g., recency lane, intent anchors, verified facts) inserted as compressed snippets will recover ~70–90% of user-visible continuity while reducing tokens by 40–70% vs full history.

Feature sketch (rough):
- Server-side 'chorus' builder that runs after each session close (or periodically) and extracts candidate snippets via lightweight heuristics + optional micro-evals.
- Lanes concept: each lane is a semantically coherent set (e.g. last-turn summary, pinned facts, user profile diffs, ongoing task list). Lanes are scored (freshness, importance).
- API surface: when calling /v1/chat/complete, a client can pass chorus=enabled and chorus_policy (max_token_budget, lane_whitelist, encryption=on/off) OR we auto-attach for customers on certain tiers.
- Compression strategies: single-sentence extraction, abstractive short-summary (1–2 lines), and pointer tokens (id references for private deployments).
- Privacy: retention windows, opt-out, per-tenant KMS for private deployments. Choruses should be treated as user data with audit logging.

User stories / acceptance (examples):
1) As a messaging app dev, I want partial continuity so a user who opens a new session still gets correct task context without me sending full chat logs.
   - Acceptance: For sample user flows, model keeps task identifiers correctly 85% of the time in A/B vs baseline.
2) As an enterprise security owner, I want choruses encrypted and visible in audit logs so we can meet compliance.
   - Acceptance: Private deploy + KMS toggle works end-to-end and logs show chorus creation events.
3) As a product manager, I want predictable token spend so I can set a budget per-session for chorus attachment.
   - Acceptance: System enforces max_token_budget and rejects additional lanes beyond budget with explicit response header.

Telemetry / metrics to track:
- Continuity retention metric: fraction of conversations that maintain key entity references (NER/QA checks).
- Token delta per-session with/without chorus.
- Latency delta for first-token and tail when chorus attached.
- User opt-outs rate and retention window compliance.
- Lane hit rates and per-lane quality score (micro-eval).

Implementation notes / sketch:
- Candidate extractor lives as a small pipeline in the serving runtime PostSession hook (or in a background worker).
- Use a tight template for abstractive summaries to keep model calls cheap: "one-line summary: <...>". Consider rule-based extraction for low-cost lane types (recency/facts).
- Store choruses in per-tenant KV (encrypted). Each chorus entry has lane metadata, score, created_at, retention_ttl.
- For Hosted: offer both stored choruses and ephemeral inline chorus generation. For Private: store only references and let customer sync.
- Rollout gating: start as opt-in beta on dev accounts, then A/B to high-usage customers.

Risks / open questions:
- How to measure 'quality' without expensive evals? Quick hack: a lightweight QA probe that asks a set of anchor questions against the model response.
- Interaction with KV cache and batching — chorus attachment might increase request size and affect batching strategy. Need SLO experiments.
- Abuse vectors: users could store sensitive PII in pinned lanes. Ensure strong redaction tools and retention defaults.
- Costs: where do we run the chorus builder? On-hosted cheap inference or as a background CPU worker?

API contract sketches (informal):
- POST /v1/chat/complete?chorus=attach 
  body: { messages: [...], chorus_policy: { max_tokens: 200, lanes: ["recency","pins"], freshness_seconds: 86400 } }
- Response headers: X-Chorus-Attached: true, X-Chorus-Tokens: 120
- Admin API: GET /v1/tenants/{id}/choruses -> list lane metadata (for console).

Console / UX ideas:
- Small panel in Redwood Console per-tenant that shows active lanes, token cost estimate, retention policy, and quick-disable toggle.
- Per-session view: preview the chorus snippets that will be attached (for debugging).

Experimental plan / milestones:
- Spike (2 wks): implement a minimal extractor that produces 3 lane types (recency, summary, pins) with rule-based extracts. Build micro-eval probe harness.
- Beta (6 wks): integrate with hosted API as opt-in flag, collect telemetry, run A/B tests on 10 customers.
- Iteration (8 wks): refine lane scoring, add abstractive short summaries for high-quality lanes, build Console UX.

Notes on dev work / tickets to spawn:
- Spike ticket: RDR-chorus-spike (extractors + micro-eval harness) -> attach to post-session worker.
- API ticket: RDR-chorus-api (query params + headers + error codes).
- Console: RDR-chorus-console (lane view + toggles).
- Security: RDR-chorus-kms (KMS integration + audit events).

Short-term experiments I can run locally:
- Create a small dataset of 200 session pairs (new session after prior session). Try rule-based recency extract vs 3-shot prompt small model to create 1-sentence lane summaries. Measure QA recall for anchors.
- Compare tokens added vs full history for each sample.

Open heuristics decisions (need input):
- Lane types initial default: {recency, pinned_facts, intent_anchor, persona_note}? (which to include by default for hosted free-tier?)
- Default retention: 7 days vs 30 days for paid? Regulatory implications for EU customers.
- Should lane generation happen synchronously (adds latency) or asynchronously (attach next request)?

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Run the local spike this week (data + micro-eval).
- Draft a short one-pager for PM sync with illustrative token/quality charts.
- Loop in Kai for private deploy KMS nuances and Evan for cost SLO forecasts.

Random brainstorm ideas / nice-to-haves:
- 'Chorus stitching' across accounts (shared workspace context) with explicit consent tokens.
- Lane-templates marketplace (customers choose lane types and quality vs cost profile).
- Automatic lane pruning via model uncertainty signal.

Notes to self: keep the initial surface small. Avoid adding abstractive lanes by default unless we have cheap micro-eval. Keep opt-outs prominent.
